tool.title: Record what the publish branch served
tool.description: Append one entry to the render log on the publish branch: what was published or taken down, when, from which commit, and — for a removal or a retention — WHY. The log is the only place a preview that vanished leaves a trace.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: A checkout of the publish branch, or a publish directory about to become one. This tool NEVER fetches, commits or pushes: the calling workflows hold the checkout with their own retry and concurrency handling, and a second pusher racing them could lose a deploy.

inputs.name: event
inputs.description: `rendered`, `removed`, `restored` or `retained`. `retained` records a removal CONSIDERED and refused, which would otherwise leave no trace.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: What was rendered — `staging-preview`, `site`, `export`. Open, not an enum: the publish branch carries more than previews, and an enum would make logging a new kind wait on a schema change.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: The path on the publish branch. Checked as a VALUE, never trusted by provenance: the slug sanitiser can emit `..`, which is only safe for a slug taken from a git ref, and a dispatch input is not one.

inputs.name: slug
inputs.description: The staging slug, where the subject has one.

inputs.name: branch
inputs.description: The branch the render came from.

inputs.name: commit
inputs.description: The commit the artefact was built from.

inputs.name: run
inputs.description: The workflow run that wrote this, so a reader can open the log.

inputs.name: prose
inputs.description: One JSON object on STDIN: `{summary, reason?, detail?, format?}`. `summary` is required and one line. `reason` is required by the SCRIPT for `removed` and `retained`, because an entry saying an artefact went and not why is the ambiguity the log exists to prevent. `format` declares how the prose reads (absent means plain text, never sniffed). Build it with `jq -n --arg`, never by concatenation.

outputs.name: entry
outputs.description: The day's JSONL the entry was APPENDED to. Append is the only verb: there is no `--remove`, no `--edit` and no `--id`, so a takedown is a `removed` ENTRY rather than the erasure of the `rendered` one before it, and the never-delete rule is structural rather than a guard every cleanup path must remember.

selection.when: Whenever something is published to or removed from the publish branch — including a removal that was refused. Called from `feature-staging.yml` at four points; `staging-render-log.bpmn` is the process.
selection.limits: It writes into a directory and does not push, so a caller that forgets to commit the log has written nothing durable. It cannot edit or delete an entry, by design. `--summary` / `--reason` / `--detail` are REFUSED as flags at exit 2 rather than ignored: they go on stdin, and a caller still passing them is told instead of silently logging an entry with no summary.

$comment.comment:
The whole reason this node exists, and why it took a change to the
script rather than a cleverer type.

── The publish branch's own history of what it served ───────────────

Bean `ru6i`. This node could not be written at all until `render-log.ts`
took its prose on stdin: `satisfies` needs a skill, the skill is
`render-logging`, and `check:tools` refuses a `Text` input that is a
command-line word. The type system was fail-closed and correct, and the
script's interface was what had to move.
